discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC by the ATLAS and CMS experiments
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism; the experimental achievement that made it real remains unrecognised. Peter Jenni (founding spokesperson of ATLAS) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders of CMS) conceived, designed and led for two decades the detectors that in 2012 discovered a scalar boson near 125 GeV and then established its spin-parity and couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and, recently, muons. These measurements turned electroweak symmetry breaking from a hypothesis into a precisely tested part of nature, and today anchor every effective-field-theory analysis of physics beyond the Standard Model. Their detector concepts, from the ATLAS toroid and calorimetry to the CMS solenoid and crystal calorimeter, made the diphoton and four-lepton discovery channels possible. This is a landmark discovery in fundamental physics, and its architects deserve the Prize.
